Name: Shrine of Bibi Pak Daman
year_built: 681 CE / c. 63 AH (popular tradition) — see note; second tradition dates the events to the early 13th century CE
year_built_note: Founded/Opened gives 681, matching the Description's 'traditional founding date of about 63 AH' under the popular Karbala-descent tradition (the six women as companions of the Ahl al-Bayt fleeing Karbala, 61 AH). A second tradition, held by the shrine's custodial family and cited scholars (Ghulam Sarwar, Ghulam Dastgir Nami, Hafeez Ullah Manzar), holds the six were daughters of Sayyid Ahmad Tokhta Tirmidhi (d. c. 602 AH) and died during the Mongol sack of Lahore in the early 13th century CE — roughly five centuries after the popular date. The Description's own 'Long Debate' section lays out the case against the Karbala dating (Islam did not reach Lahore until Mahmud of Ghazni, 11th century CE; Ali's wife Umm al-Banin is recorded with no daughter). Not resolvable from this source; the Description reports both traditions rather than choosing one. Most recent renovation of the complex: 2024.
